G3800.def:
ὄψώνιον, -ου, τό
(ὀψον- see: ὀψάριον— and ὠνέομαι), [in LXX: I Esther 4:56, 1Ma.3:28 1Mac 14:32 * ;] 
__1. provisions, provision-money, soldiers' pay: Luc 3:14, 1 Corinthiens 9:7. 
__2. Generally, wages, hire: 2 Corinthiens 11:8; ὄ. τῆς ἁμαρτίας, Romains 6:23 (see Deiss, BS, 148, 266).†

G3802.def:
παγιδεύω
(παγίς), [in LXX: 1 Rois 28:9 (נָקַשׁ hith.), Ecclésiaste 9:12 (יָקֹשׁ pu.)* ;] 
to ensnare: metaphorically, with accusative, ἐν λόγῳ, Matthieu 22:15 (not elsewhere).†

G3803.def:
παγίς, -ίδος, ή
(πήγνυμι), [in LXX for פַּח, מוֹקֵשׁ, רֶשֶׁת, etc. ;] 
poët. (Aristoph., al.) and late for πάγη, a trap, snare; metaphorically (as also in cl.): Luc 21:35, Romains 11:9" (LXX) 1 Timothée 3:7 6:9, 2 Timothée 2:26.†

G3804.def:
πάθημα, -τος, τό
(πάσχω), like πάθος, 
__1. that which befalls one, a suffering, affliction: pl., Romains 8:18, 2 Corinthiens 1:6-7, Colossiens 1:24, 2 Timothée 3:11, Hébreux 2:10 10:32, 1 Pierre 5:9; of Christ's sufferings: τὰ εἰς Χ., 1 Pierre 1:11; τ. Χριστσῦ, 1 Pierre 5:1; id. as shared by Christians, 2 Corinthiens 1:5, Philippiens 3:10, 1 Pierre 4:13. 
__2. a passive emotion, affection, passion: Galates 5:24; τ. ἀμαρτιῶν, Romains 7:5 
__3. = τὸ πάσχειν, an enduring or suffering: with genitive obj., Hébreux 2:9.†
SYN.: see: πάθος

G3805.def:
παθητός, -ή, -όν
(πάσχω), 
__1. one who has suffered. 
__2. subject to suffering (R, mg., see M, Pr., 222) or destined to suffer (AV, R, txt.): Actes 26:23.†

G3806.def:
πάθος, -ους, τό
(πάιτχω), [in LXX: Job 30:31 (אֵבֶל), Proverbes 25:20, and very frequently in (4Ma.1:1 n, al.)* ;] 
like πάθημα; 
__1. that which befalls one, that which one suffers 
__2. a passive emotion or affection (esp. of violent emotion), a passion, passionate desire; in NT always in bad sense: Colossiens 3:5; π. ἀτιμίας, Romains 1:26; π. ἐπιθυμίας, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:5.†
SYN.: π. = πάθημα, exc. that πάθημα is the more concrete and particular. In NT usage, π. represents the passive, ungoverned aspect of evil desire, as opposite to ἐπιθυμία, which is the active and also the more comprehensive term (see Tr., Syn., LXXxvii); cf. also ὄρεξις

G3807.def:
παιδαγωγός, -oῦ, ὁ
(παῖς, ἄγω), 
a guide, guardian, trainer of boys, a tutor (disting. from διδάσκαλος, Xen., Lac., 3, 1), usually a trusty slave: opposite to πατήρ, 1 Corinthiens 4:15; figuratively, of the Law, π. εἰς Χριστόν, Galates 3:24-25.†

G3808.def:
παιδάριον, -ου, τό dimin. of παῖς, 
[in LXX chiefly for נַעַר ;] 
a little boy, a lad (in late and colloq. Gk. the word seems to be used with greater latitude and even to lose its dimin. force entirely; cf. Tob.6:2-3, and see MM, xviii): Jean 6:9.†
SYN.: see: παῖς

G3809.def:
παιδεία (-ία, Τ), -ας, ἡ
(παιδεύω), [in LXX chiefly for מוּסָר ;] 
__1. the rearing of a child (Æsch.). 
__2. training, learning, instruction (Plat., al.): Éphésiens 6:4, 2 Timothée 3:16. 
__3. As in LXX (Proverbes 3:11 15:5, al.), chasten­ing, discipline: Hébreux 12:5 (LXX), Hébreux 12:7-8, 11.†

G3810.def:
παιδευτής, -οῦ, ὁ
(παιδεύω), [in LXX: Osée 5:2 (מוּסָר), Sir.37:19, 4Ma.5:34 4Mac 9:6 * ;] 
__1. prop., a teacher, instructor: Romains 2:20. 
__2. a corrector, one who disciplines (cf. Ho, l.with) : Hébreux 12:9.†

G3811.def:
παιδεύω
(παίς), [in LXX chiefly for יָסַר ;] 
__1. as in cl., to train children, hence, generally, to teach, instruct: Actes 7:22 22:3, 1 Timothée 1:20, Tite 2:12. 
__2. As in LXX (Psaumes 6:2, Proverbes 19:18, Wis.3:5, al., and for prob. ex. from π., see MM, xviii), to chasten, correct, chastise: Luc 23:16, 22, 2 Timothée 2:25, Hébreux 12:7, 10; of divine chastening, 1 Corinthiens 11:32, 2 Corinthiens 6:9, Hébreux 12:6, Apocalypse 3:19.†
SYN.: διδάσκω, q.v

G3812.def:
παιδιόθεν
(παιδίον), 
adv., [in LXX: Genèse 47:3 * ;] 
= cl. ἐκ παιδός, παιδίον, from childhood: Marc 9:21.†

G3813.def:
παιδίον, -ου, τό dimin, of παῖς, 
[in LXX chiefly for יֶלֶד, also for נַעַר, בֵּן, etc., frequently in To in ref. to full-grown youth ;] 
a young child, a little one: Matthieu 2:8-9, 11, ff., Luc 1:59, 66 1:76, 80 2:17, 27 2:40, Jean 16:21, Hébreux 11:23; of older children, Matthieu 18:2, 4-5, Marc 5:39-41 7:30 9:24, 36, Luc 9:47-48 18:17, Jean 4:49; in pl., Matthieu 11:16 14:21 15:38 18:3 19:13-14, Marc 7:28 10:13 ff., Luc 7:32 11:7 18:16, Hébreux 2:13-14 Metaphorical, 1 Corinthiens 14:20. Colloq. in familiar address (as Eng. colloq., "lads "-see M, Pr., 170n and Irish use of "boys"): Jean 21:5, 1 Jean 2:13 Jn 2:18 Jn 3:7 †
SYN.: see: παῖς

G3814.def:
παιδίσκη, -ης, ἡ dimin, of παῖς, 
[in LXX for שִׁפְחָה, אָמָה, etc. ;] 
__1. a young girl, a maiden (נַעֲרָה, Ruth 4:12). 
__2. Colloq., a young female slave, a maid-servant (see Kennedy, Sources, 40 f.; Deiss., LAE, 186, 332.2): Matthieu 26:69, Marc 14:66, 69, Luc 12:45 22:56, Jean 18:17, Actes 12:13 16:16; of Hagar, Galates 4:22-23, 30" (LXX) ; id., metaphorically, Galates 4:31.†
SYN.: see: παῖς

G3815.def:
παίζω
(παῖς), [in LXX: Genèse 21:9 26:8, Exode 32:6 (צָחַק pi.); and more frequently (Juges 16:25, al.) for (שָׂחַק pi. ;] 
prop., to play as a child, hence, generally, to play (as with singing and dancing) : 1 Corinthiens 10:7 (LXX) (cf. ἐμ-παίζω).†

G3816.def:
παῖς, genitive, παιδός, ὁ, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for עֶבֶד, also for נַעַר, נַעֲרָה, etc. ;] 
__1. a child, boy, youth, maiden: ὁ π., Matthieu 17:18, Luc 2:43 9:42, Actes 20:12; ἡ π. Luc 8:51, 54 (on the artic. fern, of address, see M, Pr., 70 f., 235; B1., § 33, 4); pl., Matthieu 2:16 21:15; of parentage, with genitive, Jean 4:51 
__2. Like Heb. עֶבֶד, Lat. Auer, Fr. garcon, Eng. boy (Æsch., Aristoph., Xen., al.), servant, slave, attendant: Matthieu 8:6, 8 8:13 Luc 7:7 12:45 15:26; in late writers (Diod., LXX: Genèse 41:37, al.), of a king's attendant or minister : Matthieu 14:2; so (= Heb. יְהוָֹה עֶבֶד) π. τ. θεοῦ (Psaumes 69:18, Ésaïe 41:8, Wis.2:13, al.), of Israel, Luc 1:54; of David, Luc 1:69, Actes 4:25; of Jesus (but see Dalman, Words, 277 f.), Matthieu 12:18 (LXX), Actes 3:13, 26 4:27, 30.†
SYN.: 
__1. τέκνον, child, with emphasis on parentage and the consequent community of nature; υἱός, son, with emphasis on the privileged position of heirship; π. refers both to age and parentage, but with emphasis on the former. Cf. also (παιδάριον), (παιδίον), (παιδίσκη), and see Westc. on 1 Jean 3:1. 
__2. see: θεράπων, and cf. Thackeray, Gr., 7 f

G3817.def:
παίω 
[in LXX chiefly for נָכָה hi. ;] 
to strike, smite: with the hand or fist, Matthieu 26:68, Luc 22:64; with a sword, Marc 14:47, Jean 18:10; of a reptile, to sting: Apocalypse 9:5.†

G3819.def:
πάλαι 
adv. of time, [in LXX: Ésaïe 48:5, 7 (אָז), etc. ;] 
long ago, of old, in time past (denoting past time absolutely, as πρότερον relatively) : Matthieu 11:21, Luc 10:13, Hébreux 1:1, Ju 4; as adj., with art., 2 Pierre 1:9; of time just past, Marc 6:47 (WH, mg.), Marc 15:44 (WH, mg., R, txt.); with durst. praes. (RV, all this time), 2 Corinthiens 12:19.†

G3820.def:
παλαιός, -ά, -όν
(πάλαι), [in LXX: Lévitique 25:22 26:10, Cantique des cantiques 7:13 (14) (יָשֵׁן), יָשֵׁן), Josué 9:4-5, Jérémie 38:11 (בָּלֶה), etc. ;] 
old, ancient; opposite to νέος, καινός: οἶνος, Luc 5:3; διαθήκη, 2 Corinthiens 3:14; ἐντολή, 1 Jean 2:7; ζύμη, 1 Corinthiens 5:7-8; ὁ π. ἄςθρωπος (for similar phrases, see Westc., Eph., 68), Romains 6:6, Éphésiens 4:22, Colossiens 3:9; neut. pl., καινὰ καὶ π., Matthieu 13:52; of things not merely old, but worn by use (as Jo, l.with, LXX), Matthieu 9:16-17, Marc 2:21-22, Luc 5:36-37.†
SYN.: see: ἀρχαῖος

G3822.def:
παλαιόω, -ῶ
(παλαιός), [in LXX chiefly for בָּלָה, pi., in pass. for בִּי qal. ;] 
to make or declare old: Hébreux 8:13; pass., to become old: of things worn out by time and use (cf. Jean 9:13, Ésaïe 50:9, al., and see: παλαιός), Luc 12:33, Hébreux 1:11" (LXX) ; τὸ παλαιούμενον, Hébreux 8:13 (where this and the act., see supr., may have the sense of abrogate, see LS, Zorell, see word).†
SYN.: γηράσκω

G3823.def:
πάλη, -ης, ἡ
(πάλλω, to sway) 
wrestling, hence, generally, fight, contest: figuratively, of the spiritual combat of Christians, Éphésiens 6:12.†

G3825.def:
πάλιν, adv., 
[in LXX for שׁוּב, etc. ;] 
__1. of place, back, backwards (LS, see word). 
__2. Of time, again, once more: Matthieu 4:8, Marc 2:13, Luc 23:20, Jean 1:35 (and freq.), Actes 17:32, Romains 11:23, Galates 1:9, Hébreux 1:6, al; pleonastically, π. ἀνακάμπτειν, Actes 18:21; ὑποστρέφειν, Galates 1:17; εἰς τὸ π., 2 Corinthiens 13:2; π. ἐκ τρίτου (Bl., §81, 4), Matthieu 26:44; ἐκ δευτέρου, Matthieu 26:42, Actes 10:15; π. δεῦτερον, Jean 4:54 21:16; π. ἄνωθεν ( Wis.19:6), Galates 4:9. 
__3. Rhetorically, again; 
__(a) further, moreover: Matthieu 5:33, Luc 13:20, Jean 12:39, al.; 
__(b) in turn, on the other hand (Soph.; LXX: Wis.13:8 16:23, al.): Luc 6:43, 1 Corinthiens 12:21, 2 Corinthiens 10:7, 1 Jean 2:8.

G3826.def:
πανπληθεί (Rec. παμπλ-, see WH, App., 150), 
adv. (πᾶς, πλῆθος), 
= cl. παμπληθές, with the whole multitude, all together: Luc 23:18.†

G3828.def:
Παμφυλία, -ας, ἡ 
Pamphylia, a province of Asia Minor: Actes 2:10 13:13 14:24 15:38 27:5.†

G3829.def:
παν-δοχεῖον (-δοκίον, Τ), -ου, τό 
(πανδοχεύς), 
late form of Att.. πανδοκεῖον, 
an inn (khân, caravanserai): Luc 10:34.†

G3830.def:
παν-δοχεύς, -έως, ὁ
(πᾶς, δέχομαι), 
late form of the Att.. πανδοκεύς (T, in l), 
an innkeeper, host: Luc 10:35.†

G3832.def:
πανοικεί (Rec., LTr., -κί), adv. 
(πᾶς, οἶκος), a word rejected by strict Atticists, though found once in Plat. (Eryx., 392c); [in LXX: Exode 1:1 (בַּיִת), 3Ma.3:27 (where A in each case reads -κίᾳ, the Attic form, cf. Genèse 50:8, al.)* ;] 
with all the household: Actes 16:34.†

G3833.def:
πανοπλία, -ας, ἡ
(πᾶς, ὅπλον) [in LXX: 2 Rois 2:21 (חֲלִיצָה), Job 39:20, Jdth.14:3, Wis.5:17, Sir.46:6, 1-2; 4Mac.6* ;] 
full armour: Luc 11:22; metaphorically (cf. Wis, l.with), τ. θεοῦ, Éphésiens 6:11, 13 †

G3834.def:
πανουργία, -ας, ἡ
(πανοῦργος), [in LXX: Josué 9:4, Proverbes 1:4 8:5 (עׇרְמָה), Nombres 24:22, Sir.19:25 21:22 31:10 (Sir.34:10) (in all cases in good or indifferent sense)* ;] 
cleverness, in cl. nearly always in bad sense, craftiness, cunning, knavery: Luc 20:23, 1 Corinthiens 3:19 (LXX, φρόνησις, for עׇרְמָה) 2 Corinthiens 4:2 11:3, Éphésiens 4:14.†

G3837.def:
πανταχοῦ 
adv., [in LXX: Ésaïe 42:22 (כָּלַם)* ;] 
everywhere: Marc 1:28 16:20, Luc 9:6, Actes 17:30 24:3 28:22, 1 Corinthiens 4:17.†

G3838.def:
παντελής, -ές
(πᾶς, τέλος), [in LXX: 3Ma.7:16 A* ;] 
all-complete, entire, perfect; εἰς τ. παντελές, completely, utterly: Luc 13:11, Hébreux 7:25 (where perhaps in temp. sense, finally; see MM, xviii).†

G3839.def:
πάντῃ (Rec. -τη), 
adv. (πᾶς), [in LXX: Sir.50:22, 3Ma.4:1 * ;] 
every way, entirely: Actes 24:3.†

G3840.def:
πάντοθεν 
adv. (πᾶς), [in LXX: Jérémie 48:31 (כֹּל), al. ;] 
from all sides: Marc 1:45, Luc 19:43, Hébreux 9:4.†

G3841.def:
παντοκράτωρ, -ορος, ὁ
(πᾶς, κρατέω), [in LXX: frequently in Job 5:8, 17, al. (שַׁדַּי), and for צָבָא, in the phrase θεός (κυρίος) π., 2 Rois 5:10, al., and frequently in Am, Za, Ma; also in Wis.7:25, Sir.42:17 50:14, 17 and frequently in Jth 2, 3Mac ;] 
almighty: 2 Corinthiens 6:18, Apocalypse 1:8 4:8 11:17 15:3 16:7, 14 9:6, 15 21:22.†

G3842.def:
πάντοτε 
adv. 
of time 
(πᾶς), [in LXX: Wis.11:21 19:18 * ;] 
in late writers (once in Arist.) for διαπαντός, ἑκάστοτε, at all times, always: Matthieu 26:11, Marc 14:7, Luc 15:31, Jean 6:34, Romains 1:10, and frequently in Paul. Epp

G3844.def:
παρά, prep. with genitive, dative, accusative, 
with radical sense, beside. 
__I. C. genitive of person(s), from the side of, from beside, from, indicating source or origin, [in LXX for מֵאֵצֶל ,מִיַד ,מִלִּפְנֵי ;] after verbs of motion, Marc 14:43, Luc 8:49, Jean 15:26, al.; after verbs of seeking, receiving, hearing, etc., Marc 8:11 12:2, Jean 4:9, 52 10:18, Philippiens 4:18, 2 Timothée 1:18, Jacques 1:7, al.; after passive verbs, of the agent (like ὑπό), Matthieu 21:42, Marc 12:11, Luc 1:37; absol., οἱ παρ᾽ αὐτοῦ, his family, his kinsfolk, Marc 3:21 (cf. M, Pr., 106f.; Field, Notes, 25f.; Swete, in l.); τὰ παρ᾽ αὐτῆς (αὐτῶν, ὑμῶν, one's means, wealth, Marc 5:26, Luc 10:7, Philippiens 4:18. 
__II. C. dative of person(s) (exc. Jean 19:25, π. τ. σταυρῷ), by the side of, beside, by, with, [in LXX for בְּעֵינֵי ,בְּיַד ,אֵצֶל ;] Luc 11:37 19:7, Jean 1:40 4:40, Actes 28:14, al.; παρ᾽ ἑαυτῷ, at home, 1 Corinthiens 16:2; with dative pl., among, Matthieu 22:25, Colossiens 4:16, al.; metaphorically, Matthieu 19:26, Marc 10:27, Luc 1:30, Romains 2:13, Jacques 1:27, al. 
__III. C. accusative, of motion by or towards, [in LXX for בְּעֵבֶר ,עַל יַד ,אֵצֶל ;] 
__1. of place, by the side of, beside, by, along: Actes 10:32, Hébreux 11:12; after verbs of motion, Matthieu 4:18, Marc 4:4, Luc 8:5, Actes 4:35, al.; after verbs of rest, Matthieu 13:1, Marc 5:21, Luc 8:35, al. 
__2. beside, beyond, metaphorically; 
__(a) beyond, against, contrary to: Actes 18:13, Romains 1:26 4:18 11:24, al.; except, 2 Corinthiens 11:24; 
__(b) beyond, above, in comparison with: Luc 3:13, Romains 12:3 14:5, Hébreux 1:4, 9 3:3, al.; 
__(with) on account of: 1 Corinthiens 12:15, 16. 
__IV. In composition: beside, to (παραλαμβάνω, παράγω), at hand (πάρειμι), from (παραρρέω), amiss (παρακούω), past (παρέρχομαι), compared with (παρομοιάζω), above measure (παροργίζω).

G3845.def:
παρα-βαίνω 
[in LXX for סוּר, עָבַר, פָּרַר, שָׂטָה, etc. ;] 
__1. in Hom. (twice), to go by the side of, stand beside. 
__2. In Æsch., Herod., Thuc., al., to go past or pass over, chiefly metaphorically, to overstep, violate, transgress (Josué 7:11, Eze.16:59, Sir.40:14, al.) : τ. παράδοσιν, Matthieu 15:2; τ. ἐντολήν, Matthieu 15:3; before ἀπό (as מִן סוּר, Deutéronome 17:20, al.), to turn aside, fall away (cf. π. τῆς ἀληθείας, Arist., Cael., i, 5, 2): Actes 1:25.†

G3846.def:
παρα-βάλλω 
[in LXX: Proverbes 2:2 4:20 5:1, 13 22:17 (נָטָה hi.), Ruth 2:16 (שָׁלַל), 2Ma.14:38 (elsewhere as seel.4)* ;] 
__1. to throw to or beside, as fodder to horses (Hom., al.). 
__2. to lay beside, compare (Hdt., Plat., al.): Marc 4:30, Rec. 
__3. Reflexive, to betake oneself, come near; of seamen, to cross over: εἰς Σάμον, Actes 20:15. 
__4. In mid. = παραβολεύομαι, which see†

G3847.def:
παρά-βασις, -εως, ἡ
(παραβαίνω), [in LXX: Psaumes 101:3 (שֵׂט), 4Ki.2:24 A, Wis.14:31, 2Ma.15:10 * ;] 
__1. a going aside, a deviation (Arist.). 
__2. In later writers, an overstepping; metaphorically, transgression (Plut., al.) : Romains 4:15 5:14, Hébreux 2:2 9:15; τ. νόμου, Romains 2:23; ἐν π., 1 Timothée 2:14; τ. παραβάσεων χάριν, Galates 3:19 
SYN.: see: ἁμαρτία

G3848.def:
παρα-βάτης, -ου, ὁ
(παραβαίνω), [in Sm.: Psaumes 17:4 139:19, Jérémie 6:28 * ;] 
__1. one who stands beside, the warrior who stands by the charioteer (of. παραβαίνω, 1). 
__2. a transgressor (Æsch., παρβάτης): Galates 2:18, Jacques 2:9; π. νόμου, Romains 2:25, 27, Jacques 2:11.†

G3849.def:
παρα-βιάζομαι 
[in LXX: Genèse 19:9, 4Ki.2:17 (פָּצַר), Deutéronome 1:43 (זוּד hi.), 1 Rois 28:23 (פָּרַץ) see1. 4 * ;] 
__1. prop., to force against nature or law. 
__2. to compel by force (Polyb.). 
__3. to constrain by entreaty (Ge, 1Sam, ll. with): Luc 24:29, Actes 16:15.†

G3850.def:
παραβολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(παραβάλλω), [in LXX (cf. McNeile, Mt., 185): Nombres 23:7, Deutéronome 28:37, Psaumes 44:14, Proverbes 1:6, Eze.12:22, al. (מָשַׁל), Sir.47:17 (חִידָה), al. mutt. in Sir, Wis.5:3 ;] 
__1. a placing beside, juxtaposition (Polyb., al.). 
__2. a comparing, comparison (Plat., Arist., al.). 
__3. a comparison, illustration, analogy, figure (Arist., al.) : Matthieu 24:32, Marc 3:23, Hébreux 9:9 11:19; specif. of the pictures and narratives drawn from nature and human life which are characteristic of the synoptic teaching of our Lord, a parable: Matthieu 13:3, 10 Marc 4:2, 10, Luc 8:4, 9-11, al.; with genitive ref., Matthieu 13:18, 36 
__4 4 Like Heb. מָשַׁל (1 Rois 10:12, Proverbes 1:6, Sir.3:29, al.), = παροιμία, a proverb or gnomic saying: Luc 4:23 5:36 6:39 
SYN.: παροιμία (see Abbott, Essays, 82 ff.)

G3851.def:
παρα-βολεύομαι
= cl. παραβάλλομαι (2Ma.14:38), 
to expose oneself to danger, hazard one's life: with dative ref., τ. ψυχῇ (see M, Pr., 64), Philippiens 2:30 (Rec. παραβουλ-). Cited by Deiss., LAE, 84, 120.†
παρα-βουλεύομαι, 
to consult amiss, or perh. (see LS, see word), a vulg. form of παρα-βολ- (which see) : Philippiens 2:30, Rec.†

G3852.def:
παρ-αγγελία, -ας, ἡ
(παραγγέλλω), 
an instruction, charge, com­mand: Actes 5:28 16:24, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:2, 1 Timothée 1:5 1:18. (In Xen., Polyb., of a military order.)†

G3853.def:
παρ-αγγέλλω
(παρά, ἀγγὲλλω), [in LXX for שָׁמַע pi., hi., etc. ;] 
__1. to transmit a message (Æsch., Eur.). 
__2. to order, command (Hdt., Xen., al.) : with inf., Actes 15:5; with accusative of thing(s), 1 Corinthiens 11:17, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:4, 1 Timothée 4:11 5:7; before ἵνα (M, Pr., 207; Bl., § 69, 4), Marc 6:8, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:12; with dative of person(s), Actes 17:30 R, txt., 1 Thessaloniciens 4:11; before λέγων, Matthieu 10:5; with inf. aor., Matthieu 15:35, Marc 8:6, Luc 8:29, Actes 10:42 16:18 (aoristic pres.; see M, Pr., 119); id. with neg., μή, Luc 5:14 8:56, Actes 23:22, 1 Corinthiens 7:10; with inf. pres., Actes 16:23, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:6; id. with neg., ιή, Luc 9:21, Actes 1:4 4:18 5:28, 40, 1 Timothée 1:3 6:17; with accusative, τοῦτο, before ὅτι (E1., § 70, 3), 2 Thessaloniciens 3:10; with accusative and inf., Actes 23:30, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:6, 1 Timothée 6:13 (Bl., § 72, 5).†
SYN.: see: ἐντέλλω

G3854.def:
παρα-γίνομαι
(Ion. and late for -γίγν-), [in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא ;] 
__1. to be beside or at hand (Hom., Hdt., al.), hence, to stand by, sup­port (Æsch., Thuc., al.) : with dative of person(s), 2 Timothée 4:16. 
__2. to come, come up, arrive (Hdt., Xen., al., and frequently in later writers; see MM, xviii; Thackeray, Gr., 267.2): absol., Luc 14:21 19:16, Jean 3:23, Actes 5:21-22, 25 9:39 10:32-33 11:23 14:27 17:10 18:27 21:18 23:16, 35 24:17, 24 25:7 28:21, 1 Corinthiens 16:3; before εἰς, Jean 8:2, Actes 9:26 15:4; ἐπί, with accusative, Luc 22:52; πρός, with accusative, Luc 7:4, 20 8:19, Actes 20:18; id. before ἐκ, Luc 11:6; παρά, with genitive, Marc 14:43; ἀπὸ . . . εἰς, Matthieu 2:1, Actes 13:14; ἀπὸ . . . ἐπὶ . . . πρός, Matthieu 3:13; of a teacher coming forward in public: Matthieu 3:1, Luc 12:51, Hébreux 9:11.†

G3855.def:
παρ-άγω 
[in LXX chiefly for עָבַר ;] 
__1. trans., to lead by, lead aside, lead into, lead forward, etc. 
__2. Intrans., 
__(a) to pass by: Matthieu 9:9, 27 20:30, Marc 2:14 15:21, Jean 8:59 R, txt., Jean 9:1; before παρό, with accusative, Marc 1:16; 
__(b) to go away, depart; metaphorically, to pass away: 1 Corinthiens 7:31; mid., 1 Jean 2:8 Jn 2:17.†

G3856.def:
παρα-δειγματίζω
(δείκνυμι), [in LXX: Nombres 25:4 (יָקַע hi.), Jérémie 13:22 (חָמַס ni.), Eze.28:17 (רַאֲוָה), Esther 4:17, Dan LXX 2:5 * ;] 
to set forth as an example; in bad sense, to put to open shame: Hébreux 6:6 (Polyb., Plut., al.).†

G3857.def:
παράδεισος, -ου, ὁ
(an Oriental word, first used by Xen. of the parks of Persian kings and nobles) [in LXX chiefly for גַּן, Genèse 1:8 ff., al.; also for עֵדֶן, Ésaïe 51:3; פַּרְדֵּס, Néhémie 2:8, Ecclésiaste 2:5 ;] 
__1. a park, pleasure-ground, garden (LXX), an orchard (in π., see MM, ii, xviii; Deiss., BS, 148). 
__2. Paradise, the abode of the blessed dead: Luc 23:43, 2 Corinthiens 12:4, Apocalypse 2:7.†

G3859.def:
παρα-δια-τριβή, -ῆς, ἡ 
useless wrangling: seel. in Rec. for διαπαρατριβή (which see), 1 Timothée 6:5.†
δια-παρα-τριβή, -ῆς, ἡ 
(παρατριβή, friction, irritation) 
mutual irritation (Field, Notes, 211), wrangling: 1 Timothée 6:5 (Rec. παραδιατριβή).†

G3860.def:
παρα-δίδωμι, 
[in LXX chiefly for נתן ;] correl. to παρδέχομαι, 
__1. to give or hand over to another: with accusative and dative, Matthieu 11:27 25:14, Luc 4:6, al.; of being delivered up to a course of teaching, pass. before εἰς, Romains 6:17. 
__2. to commit, commend: Actes 14:26 15:40, 1 Pierre 2:23. 
__3. to give or deliver up to prison or judgment: with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 4:12, Marc 1:14, Romains 4:25, 2 Pierre 2:4; id. before ὑπέρ, Romains 8:32; with dative, Matthieu 5:25, Marc 15:1, Luc 12:58, Jean 19:11, al.; id. before ἵνα, Jean 19:16; with inf., Actes 12:4; before εἰς, Matthieu 10:17 17:22 24:9, Luc 21:12, Actes 8:3, 2 Corinthiens 4:11, al.; τ. Σατανᾷ, 1 Timothée 1:20; id. before εἰς, 1 Corinthiens 5:5; with the collat. idea of treachery (= προδίδωμι), with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 26:25, Marc 14:11, Jean 6:64, al.; id. with dative, Matthieu 26:15, al.; present ptcp., ὁ παραδιδοὺς, Matthieu 26:25, Marc 14:42, Jean 13:11. 
__4. to hand down, hand on or deliver verbally (traditions, commands, etc.): Marc 7:13, Luc 1:2, Actes 6:14, 1 Corinthiens 11:2 15:2; pass., 2 Pierre 2:21, Ju 3. 
__5. to permit (for exx. in cl., see LS, see word): Marc 4:29.

G3861.def:
παράδοξος, -ον
(παρά, δόξα), [in LXX: Jdth.13:13, Wis.5:2 16:17 19:5, Sir.43:25; 2-4 Mac 3 * ;] 
contrary to received opinion, incredible, marvellous: pl., Luc 5:26.†
SYN.: see: δύναμις

G3862.def:
παρά-δοσις, -εως, ἡ
(παραδίδωμι), [in LXX: Esther 7:26 (אֵסוּר), Jérémie 32:4 (נָתַן ni.), Jérémie 34:2 * ;] 
__1. a handing down or over, transfer, transmission (Arist., Polyb., al., LXX). 
__2. tradition of doctrine (Plat., Epict., al.); by meton., of the doctrine itself : Matthieu 15:2-3, 6, Marc 7:3, 1 Corinthiens 11:2, Galates 1:14, Colossiens 2:8, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:15 3:9.†

G3863.def:
παρα-ζηλόω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Deutéronome 32:21, 3Ki.14:22, Psaumes 78:58 (קָנָא pi., hi.), Psaumes 37:1, 7-8 (חָרָה hith.), Sir.30:3 * ;] 
to provoke to jealousy: Romains 10:19 (LXX) Romains 11:11, 14, 1 Corinthiens 10:22.†

G3864.def:
παρα-θαλάσσιος, -α, -ον
(παρά, θάλασσα) [in LXX: Jérémie 47:7 (יָם חוֹף), etc. ;] 
by the sea: Matthieu 4:13.†

G3865.def:
παρα-θεωρέω, -ῶ 
__1. to examine side by side, compare. 
__2. to over­look, neglect: pass., Actes 6:1.†

G3866.def:
παρα-θήκη, -ης, ἡ
(παρατίθημι), [in LXX: Lévitique 6:2, 4 (Lev 5:21, 23) (פִּקָּדוֹן), and in Tob 10:13, 2Ma.3:10 2Mac 3:15, seel. for παρακαταθήκη (which see) * ;] 
a deposit or trust: 1 Timothée 6:20, 2 Timothée 1:12 1:14 (for exx. of this form, see MM, Exp., iii, xviii).†

G3867.def:
παρ-αινέω, -ω 
[in LXX: 2Ma.7:25-26, 3Ma.5:17 3Mac 7:12 * ;] 
to exhort, advise: with accusative of person(s) and inf. (see Bl., § 72, 5; M, Pr., 205), Actes 27:22; absol., before λέγων, Actes 27:9.†

G3868.def:
παρ-αιτέομαι, -οῦμαι 
[in LXX for בָּקַשׁ pi., etc. ;] 
__1. to beg of or from another: Marc 15:6 (Rec. ὅνπερ ᾐτοῦντο, see Field, Notes, 43). 
__2. to deprecate; 
__(a) prop., with neg., to entreat that not (Thuc., al.): Hébreux 12:19; 
__(b) to refuse, decline, avoid: o. accusative, 1 Timothée 4:7 5:11, 2 Timothée 2:23, Tite 3:10, Hébreux 12:25 (EV; but see Field, Notes, 234). 
__3. to beg off, ask to be excused, excuse (Polyb., al.) : Luc 14:18-19 (Hébreux 12:25, Field, l.with).†

G3869.def:
παρα-καθίζω 
[in LXX: Job 2:13 (יָשַׁב)* ;] 
to set beside; act. for mid., to sit down beside: Luc 10:39, Rec. (for -έζομαι, which see).†

G3870.def:
παρακαλέω, -ῶ, 
[in LXX chiefly for נחם ni., pi. ;] 
__1. to call to one, call for, summon: Actes 28:20 (R, mg.; R, txt., entreat); hence (of the gods: Dem., Xen., al.), to invoke, call on, beseech, entreat: τ. πατέρα μου, Matthieu 26:53; τ. κύριον, 2 Corinthiens 12:8; in late writers (Polyb., Diod., al.; rarely in LXX; in π., see Deiss., LAE, 176.14), also of men: absol., Phm 9; with accusative, Matthieu 8:5, Marc 1:40, Actes 16:9, al.; with inf., Marc 5:17, Luc 8:41, Actes 8:31, al.; before ἵνα (see M, Pr., 205, 208), Mt 14"36, Marc 5:18, Luc 8:31, al. 
__2. to admonish, exhort: absol., Luc 3:18, Romains 12:8, 2 Timothée 4:2, al.; with accusative, Actes 15:32, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:11, Hébreux 3:13, al.; id. before inf., Actes 11:23, Romains 12:1, Philippiens 4:2, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:10, al.; before ἵνα (see M, Pr., l.with), 1 Corinthiens 1:10, 2 Corinthiens 8:6, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:1, al. 
__3. to cheer, encourage, comfort (Plut., LXX: Jb 43, Ésaïe 35:3, Sir.43:24, al.): with accusative, 2 Corinthiens 1:6, Éphésiens 6:22, Colossiens 2:2, al.; id. before ἐν, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:18; διά, 2 Corinthiens 1:4; pass., Matthieu 5:4, Luc 16:25, Actes 20:12. 
SYN.: παραμυθέω (cf. M, Th., 25).

G3871.def:
παρα-καλύπτω 
[in LXX: Ésaïe 44:8 (פָּחַד), Eze.22:26 (עָלַם hi.)* ;] 
to cover by hanging something beside, to hide: metaphorically (as Plat., al.), Luc 9:45.†

G3873.def:
παρά-κειμαι 
[in LXX: Jdt.3.2-3, Sir.30:18 34:16, Dan LXX Bel 1:14, 2,3 Mac.5* ;] 
to lie beside, be near, be present: Romains 7:18, 21.†

G3874.def:
παρά-κλησις, -εως, ἡ
(παρακαλέω), [in LXX : Job 21:2, Psaumes 94:19, Osée 13:14, Nahum 3:7, Ésaïe 57:18 66:11, Jérémie 16:7 (נָחַם, its parts and derivatives), Jérémie 38:9 (תַּחֲנוּן), Ésaïe 28:29 30:7, 1Ma.10:24 1Mac 12:9, 2Ma.7:24 2Mac 15:11 * ;] 
__1. a calling to one's aid, summons (Thus.), hence, appeal, entreaty (Strab., Plut., al., 1Ma.10:24; of. Lft., Notes, 20) : 2 Corinthiens 8:4. 
__2. exhortation, encouragement: Actes 15:31, Romains 12:8, 1 Corinthiens 14:3, 2 Corinthiens 8:17, Philippiens 2:1, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:3, 1 Timothée 4:13, Hébreux 12:5; λόγος (τῆς) π., Actes 13:15, Hébreux 13:22; υἱὸς π., Actes 4:36. 
__3. consolation, comfort (Phalar., LXX) : Luc 6:24, Actes 9:31, 2 Corinthiens 1:4-7 7:4 7:7 7:13, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:16, Phm 7; τ. γραφῶν, Romains 15:4; θεὸς τῆς π., Romains 15:5, 2 Corinthiens 1:3; π. τοῦ Ἰσραήλ (see Dalman, Words, 109 f.), Lk

G3875.def:
παρά-κλητος, -ον
(παρακαλεω), [in Aq., Th.: Job 16:2 * ;] 
called to one's aid in a judicial cause (Dion. Cass.); hence, most frequently as subst., ὁ π., an advocate, pleader, intercessor (Dem., al.; so in Rabbinic lit., פְּרַקְלִיטָא), "a friend of the accused person, called to speak to his character, or otherwise enlist sympathy in his favour" (Field, Notes, 102). In NT, specif., ὁ π., 
__(a) of Christ, 1 Jean 2:1 (see ICC, Jo. Epp., 23 ff.); 
__(b) of the Holy Spirit (AV, comforter; but see opp. with), Jean 14:16, 26 15:26 16:7 (cf. also Abbott, Essays, 86, 97; Deiss., LAE, 339 f.; MM, xviii; Westc., Jo., ii, 188)

G3876.def:
παρ-ακοή, -ῆς, ἡ 
__1. a hearing amiss (Flat.)
__2. Later, as following inattention, disobedience: Romains 5:19, 2 Corinthiens 10:6, Hébreux 2:2 (cf. παρακούω, and see Tr., Syn., § lxvi).†

G3878.def:
παρ-ακούω 
[in LXX: Esther 3:3, 8 (עָבַר, עָשָׂה, with neg.) Esther 4:14 7:4 (חָרַשׁ hi.), Ésaïe 65:12 (שָׁמַע, with neg.), I Esther 4:11, Tob.3:4 * ;] 
__1. to overhear. 
__2. to hear amiss or imperfectly. 
__3. Later (as in LXX, Polyb., Plut.; also in π., see MM, xviii), to hear without heeding, take no heed: Marc 5:36; with genitive, Matthieu 18:17.†

G3879.def:
παρα-κύπτω 
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁקַף ni., hi. ;] 
__1. to stoop sideways. 
__2. to stoop to look: Luc 24:12 (R, txt.), Jean 20:5, 11, Metaphorical (see Hort, Ja., in l), to look into: before εἰς, Jacques 1:25, 1 Pierre 1:12.†

G3880.def:
παρα-λαμβάνω 
[in LXX chiefly for לָקַח, also for יָרַשׁ, etc. ;] 
__1. with accusative of thing(s), like παραδέχομαι, correl. to παραδίδωμι, to receive from another: Colossiens 4:17, Hébreux 12:28; of the mind, 1 Corinthiens 11:23 15:1 15:3, Galates 1:9, Philippiens 4:9; with inf., Marc 7:4; before παρά, with gem, Galates 1:12, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:13 4:1, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:6; τ. Χριστόν (Lft., in l), Colossiens 2:6. 
__2. C. accusative of person(s), to take to or with oneself: Matthieu 2:13-14, 20-21 17:1 26:37, Marc 4:36 5:40 9:2 10:32, Luc 9:10, 28 11:26 18:31 19:16, Actes 15:39 23:18; γυναῖκα, Matthieu 1:20, 24; μεθ᾽ ἑαυτοῦ, Matthieu 12:45 18:16, Marc 14:33; before εἰς, Matthieu 4:5, 8 27:27; κατ᾽ ἰδίαν, Matthieu 20:17; mid., before πρὸς ἐμαυτόν, Jean 14:3; pass., Matthieu 24:40-41, Luc 17:34-36; ptcp., prefixed to other verbs (Bl, § 74, 2), Actes 16:33 21:24, 26 21:32; metaphorically, Jean 1:11.†

G3881.def:
παρα-λέγω 
to lay beside; mid., 
__(a) to lie beside (Hom.); 
__(b) later, of sailors, to sail past: with accusative, Actes 27:8, 13.†

G3882.def:
παρ-άλιος, -ον
(in cl., chiefly -α, -ον), [in LXX for יָם, חוֹף, etc., with prep. ;] 
by the sea; ἡ π. (sc. χώρα, in LXX ἡ παραλία, Deutéronome 1:7, Josué 9:1, Jdth.1:7, al.), the sea coast: Luc 6:17.†

G3883.def:
παρ-αλλαγή, -ῆς, ἡ
(παραλλάσσω), [in LXX: 4Ki.9:20 (שִׁגָּעוֹן)* ;] 
in various senses (LS, see word), change: Jacques 1:17.†

G3884.def:
παρα-λογίζομαι 
[in LXX chiefly for רָמָה pi. ;] 
__1. to miscalculate. 
__2. to reason falsely, hence, to mislead: Colossiens 2:4, Jacques 1:22.†

G3885.def:
παρα-λυτικός, -ή, -όν
(παραλύω), 
paralytic: Matthieu 4:24 8:6 9:2, 6, Marc 2:3-5, 9-10 Luc 5:24 (Rec., WH, mg.).†

G3886.def:
παρα-λύω 
[in LXX: Jérémie 6:24, Jer 27:43, Eze.21:7 (רָפָה), etc. ;] 
__1. to loose from the side, set free. 
__2. to weaken, enfeeble; pass., to be en­feebled, esp. by a paralytic stroke: Luc 5:18, 24, Actes 8:7 9:33, Hébreux 12:12" (LXX) .†

G3887.def:
παρα-μένω 
[in LXX: Proverbes 12:7, Da TH Daniel 11:17 (עָמַד), etc. ;] 
to remain beside or near: Hébreux 7:23, Jacques 1:25; of remaining alive, 1 Corinthiens 16:6 (WH, κατα-), Philippiens 1:25 (cf. συμ-παραμένω).†

G3888.def:
παρα-μυθέομαι, -οῦμαι 
[in LXX: 2Ma.15:9 (Sm. 8)* ;] 
__1. to en­courage, exhort. 
__2. to comfort, console: with accusative of person(s), Jean 11:31, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:11 5:14; id. before περί, Jean 11:19.†
SYN.: παρακαλέω

G3889.def:
παραμυθία, -ας, ἡ
(παραμυθέομαι) [in LXX: Esther 8:13, Wis.19:12 * ;] 
__1. encouragement, exhortation. 
__2. comfort, consolation: 1 Corinthiens 14:3 .†
SYN.: παράκλησις

G3890.def:
παραμύθιον, -ου, τό
(παραμυθέομαι) [in LXX: Wis.3:18 * ;] 
__1. an exhortation, persuasion, encouragement: Philippiens 2:1 (cf. Plat., Legg., vi, 773 E, al.; see Lft. and ICC, Phi., l.with). 
__2. assuagement, abatement, hence, consolation (Wis, l.with, and frequently in cl.).†

G3891.def:
παρα-νομέω, ῶ
[in LXX for הָלַל, etc., chiefly in Pss and 2Mac ;] 
to be a παράνομος, to transgress the law: Actes 23:3.†

G3892.def:
παρανομία, -ας, ἡ 
[in LXX: Psaumes 37:7 (מְזִמָּה), etc. ;] 
law-breaking, transgression: 2 Pierre 2:16.†

G3893.def:
παρα-πικραίνω 
[in LXX chiefly for מָרַד qal., hi., מְרִי, most frequently in Psa and Eze ;] 
to embitter, provoke: absol. (yet sc. τ. θεόν, cf. Psaumes 106:7, Eze.2:5-8, al., and with τὸν θ. added, Psaumes 5:4, Eze.20:21, al.), Hébreux 3:16 (cf. παραπικρασμός).†

G3894.def:
παρα-πικρασμός, -οῦ, ἁ
(παραπικραίνω) [in LXX: Psaumes 95:8 (מְרִיבָה elsewhere rendered Λοιδόρησις, Exode 17:7; ἀντιλογία, Deutéronome 33:8, al.; λοιδορία, Nombres 20:24)* ;] 
provocation: ἐν τῷ π. (Heb. at Meribah), Hébreux 3:8, 15" (LXX) .†

G3895.def:
παρα-πίπτω 
[in LXX: Eze.14:13 15:8 18:24 20:27 (מָעַל), Eze.22:4 (אָשַׁם), Esther 6:10 (נָפַל hi.), Wis.6:9 12:2, 2Ma.10:4 A* ;] 
__1. most frequently (Hdt., Thuc., al.), to fall in one's way, befall. 
__2. to fall into or in (before εἰς, Polyb.; with dative, 2Mac, l.with). 
__3. to fall away (En, Wis, ll. with; in Polyb., with genitive) : absol., Hébreux 6:6. 
__4. to fail (λόγος, Es, l.with; cf. 1 Rois 3:19).†

G3896.def:
παρα-πλέω 
to sail by or past: with accusative, Actes 20:16.†

G3897.def:
παρα-πλήσιος, -α, -ον (Hdt., Plat., al.; also -ος, -ον, Thuc., Polyb.), coming near, nearly resembling. Neut. -ον, adverbially, 
= ίως, in a way nearly resembling: with dative, Philippiens 2:27.†

G3898.def:
παρα-πλησίως 
adv. (παραπλήσιος) [in Quint.: Osée 8:6 * ;] 
in like manner: Hébreux 2:14.†

G3899.def:
παρα-πορεύομαι 
[in LXX chiefly for עָבַר ;] 
__1. to go beside, accom­pany. 
__2. to go past, pass by: Matthieu 27:39, Marc 11:20 15:29; before διά, with genitive, Marc 2:23 9:30 (WH, mg.).†
